The corpus IS the byte-agreement corpus and `selfhost/emit_java.rvl` ports no stream lowering (nor do the go and rust ports), so a corpus document holding a stream would force a divergence; see the matching `unported` entry in selfhost_blind_spots.json. item 130 Slice 2 lowered the derived-stream combinator chain here (`_stream_chain` nests the `map`/`filter`/`take` links inside the subscription's acquisition and `_stream_stage_arrow` renders each pure transform against the tier's string item type); both are on the same stream-holding path and so are uncovered for the same reason. `_refuse_unlowered_stream_surface` drops from 7 to 5 because the combinator arm it used to carry is gone. `_refuse_unlowered_stream_surface` goes back from 2 to 4: item 130 §4.5 puts the `replay(…)` refusal beside the surviving `drain` one. The two are refused for different reasons — the window for the deterministic clock this tier does not carry, replay for the recovery surface (§4.9) that lives on py — and neither is reachable from a corpus document, because a stream-holding document cannot be one. Item 130's required-`Stream[T]` coeffect adds `_refuse_required_stream`, which refuses a component that declares `requires <k>: Stream[T]` on this tier: the coeffect is lowered only on the py reference, and a corpus document declaring one would be REFUSED here rather than emitted, so it cannot be a byte-agreement case. The refusal is pinned by tests/test_stream_reactive.py instead. Item 130 §4.5's last-n backlog is LOWERED on this tier now: `_refuse_unlowered_stream_surface` goes from 4 to 5 because its replay arm now tells the durable `replay(from: …)` cursor (refused) from the last-n count (lowered), and `_expr` rises by 4 for the `Stream.source(n)` and `Stream.subscribeReplay` arms. A cursor refusal document is no way out: every `.rvl` under tests/fixtures is a gate/reference census case and the native gate (selfhost/lower.rvl) false-rejects any document carrying `replay(…)`. `_refuse_deferred_emissions` and `_refuse_validated_emissions` in backends/java/emit.py are the same wrapper around a shared refusal in `revl.session_commit` and `revl.validated_boundary`. The 8 statements left in each are the `except ModuleNotFoundError` standalone-import bootstrap, which puts src/ on sys.path and imports `revl` again. It runs only when emit.py is executed as a script with `revl` not importable. That is an invocation mode, not an input, so no corpus document and no refusal document can reach it, and these 16 statements stay recorded by design rather than as backlog. The RevlError-to-EmitError translation in both wrappers used to be recorded here too and is reached now, by tests/fixtures/emit_java_refusals/deferred_emission_call.rvl and validated_emission_operation.rvl (issue #1431).
